column4: Gap 392-A — the microsoft/pybryt row keys as {python} alone, so "no PyPI release since 2022" is adjudicated against every granted Python row. The claim is "this Python thing is stale", not "no maintained Python X". Fix is a narrower lexicon entry, not a stoplist.  🔵 RE-PINNED BY p393: p393's Tier 1/3/5 inserts moved this sentence from line 123 to 133. The adjudication is unchanged; only the anchor moved.

Gap 392-G — the claim is region-PARTITIONED ("closed for Brazil, open for Mexico, EMEA and APAC") and the key set cannot express "Mexico but not Brazil": "Mexico" is a surface form of r:latam, so the Brazilian row that CLOSED half the gap refutes the half that stays open. Sub-region granularity, registered rather than reworded.  🔵 RE-PINNED BY p393: p393's North America / EMEA / APAC / LATAM inserts moved this sentence from line 1081 to 1188. The adjudication is unchanged; only the anchor moved.

Gap 393-H — p392's class 3b (a QUOTED absence must not count as a published one) is INCOMPLETELY FIXED: it handles a quote split by a colon on one line, and this quote is split by a colon AND spans a newline, so the opening quote mark is lost to the segmenter. The sentence is Pattern AA's WITHDRAWAL of p391's claim ('Note what this is and is not: p391 published "the interop edge must be a separate runtime" as a language claim and was wrong'), i.e. the gate is again reading a correction as a fresh claim — the one thing p392 wrote that a gate must never do. The prose is correct and is kept as written; the instrument is what needs the fix. Remedy named for the successor in Gap 393-H.
